annotation.title_clean: Authorizing robots with artificial intelligence to conclude legal actions
annotation.title_en: Authorizing robots with artificial intelligence to conclude legal actions
annotation.venue: Twejer (Soran University), Special Issue, ELI Conference
annotation.summary_en: Iraqi legal study asking whether AI-enabled robots (androids) can be appointed agents to conclude legal acts under agency contracts. It examines the robot's legal capacity and status, the scope of agency, and proposes legal amendments adapting Iraqi civil law to the robot's legal nature.
key_provisions_or_claims: Examines whether an AI robot can have capacity to act as an agent in an agency contract.
Analyses legal characterisation of the robot and the scope of agency, including acts exceeding authority.
Questions how a robot can assess the principal's non-material interests.
Proposes amending Iraqi legal texts to accommodate AI robots as agents.
Reviews comparative views, e.g. Saudi Arabia's citizenship for a robot.
